DELUGE: Strong 1H Profit, S$459M Order Book — And Changi T5 Still To Come
article:
Deluge Corporation has delivered a strong first set of results since its October listing.
The provider of fire protection and engineering solutions has over 4 decades of experience, and has delivered work on major infrastructure projects.

For the six months ended Sept 2026:

The star performer was the Integrated Projects segment, which includes major infrastructure, data-centre and offshore-and-marine contracts.

Revenue jumped
54.9% to S$49.1 million
, while segment profit before tax increased from just S$1.2 million to
S$9.0 million
.

Case by case

Integrated Projects' gross margin reached about
29.8%
in 1H, helped by variation orders and cost savings particularly as the Singapore-Johor Rapid Transit System project wound down.

Management said variation orders (VOs) are case-by-case.
In 1H, VOs and cost savings as the Johor Bahru–Singapore RTS Link approached completion helped lift Integrated Projects’ gross margin to 29.8%, above its normal 24%–25% range.

Deluge CEO Lee Wai Wah
Management said contract prices for projects in the order book are already locked in, while Deluge is becoming increasingly selective about new work amid margin pressure in the construction industry.

Lifecycle Services had a quieter half

Deluge’s Lifecycle Services segment is the after-sales part of the business.

After Deluge installs a fire-protection system, it can continue earning from the same building through maintenance, inspections, repairs, emergency work, system upgrades and additions & alterations (A&A) when tenants renovate or spaces are reconfigured.

John Paul Chen, Group Strategy & Investments Director, Deluge
Lifecycle Services generated
S$16.6 million of revenue and S$3.9 million of PBT
.

Gross margin fell from around 53% to about
40%
, below its historical 45%–50% range.

The reason was mainly timing: activity in higher-margin additions-and-alterations and ad-hoc maintenance work was quieter during the period.

Some such projects have already been secured for 2H, while others remain under tender.

Order book continues to grow

Despite the sharply higher project revenue, Deluge's
order book
stood at more than
S$459.1 million
as at 17 Nov, after securing more than S$147.7 million of new contracts since January across Singapore and Malaysia.
The latest awards span infrastructure, marine and offshore, residential and industrial projects, including a data centre project in Penang, demonstrating the breadth of the Group's capabilities and continued customer confidence in its engineering solutions.

Another potential catalyst is Changi Airport Terminal 5.
Management estimates the fire-protection tender comprises three packages worth an aggregate
S$350 million–S$400 million
.

Management's narrative on Deluge's competitive edge can be summed up as:

There are over 700 fire contractors in the market, but for bigger, complex jobs—like T5 —we are in a very good position. Only 8 contractors in Singapore hold the BCA ME06 L6 grading (unlimited tender limit). Very few of those L6 contractors have the track record, financial capability, and experience to handle mega-projects like Changi T5.

Results of the T5 tenders may be available in Q1 or Q2 2027, although actual work would likely commence only around 2028/29.
Deluge does not carry the same fixed-site exposure as a conventional civil contractor.
Management said its teams are mobilised only when construction sites are ready for fire-protection installation, while 30%–40% of its workforce can be outsourced during peak periods.
When one project is delayed, workers can be redeployed to another ready site.
This reduces the idle manpower and overhead burden typically associated with construction delays.

title: Dividend Windfall: 3 SGX Stocks Recently Hiking Payouts by 33%+
article:
A
bigger dividend
feels like a reward.
But the size of the increase, on its own, tells you very little.
What matters is where the extra cash came from.
A payout funded by rising profits can repeat, while one funded by a one-off gain or a timing quirk may not.
The three SGX stocks below all lifted their dividends by a third or more in their latest results.
Their reasons differ, and so do the odds of a repeat.

Note: periods differ. Tiong Woon reports a full-year final dividend; Boustead and Valuetronics report six-month interims.
Is Tiong Woon’s bigger dividend backed by cash?
Tiong Woon Corporation Holding Ltd
(SGX: BQM) is an integrated heavy lift specialist.
For the financial year ended 30 June 2026 (FY2026), the board proposed a final dividend of S$0.025 per share, up from S$0.0175 a year ago – an increase of 43%.
Profits paid for it.
Revenue rose 15% year on year (YoY) to S$187.7 million, and profit attributable to shareholders climbed 24% to S$23.9 million.
Gross margin widened to 40.7% from 37.6% as the heavy lift segment earned higher margins.
Free cash flow is the lifeblood of dividends, and Tiong Woon’s improved sharply.
The group generated S$43.7 million in free cash flow, up from S$6.3 million.
Part of that improvement came from lower spending.
Cash spent on equipment fell 47%, yet total asset additions fell only 18%.
Over the same period, other secured borrowings rose to S$64.6 million from S$53.8 million.
The group carries S$108.0 million in debt against S$86.6 million in cash and bank deposits.
Management plans to keep renewing and expanding its fleet, so spending could climb again.
The dividend also grew faster than profit this year, but that gap cannot keep widening.
Can Boustead Singapore’s dividend outgrow a profit dip?
As Singapore’s
oldest continuous business organisation
,
Boustead Singapore Limited
(SGX: F9D) runs four divisions spanning real estate solutions, geospatial technology, energy engineering and healthcare.
For the six months ended 30 September 2026 (1HFY2027), the board declared an interim dividend of S$0.02 per share, 0.5 cents higher than a year ago.
That works out to an increase of 33%.
Reported profit moved the other way.
Revenue rose 38% YoY to S$406.6 million, while profit attributable to equity holders fell 10% to S$31.5 million.
Gross margin slipped to 32% from 38%, and a higher effective income tax rate weighed on earnings.
Boustead also booked an S$8.4 million reversal of its share of net asset value after opting out of a committed capital contribution to its associate, UIB Holdings; the move diluted its stake.
Adjusted for other gains and losses, impairments and other exceptional items, net profit rose 41% to S$39.5 million.
The order book offers support.
Real Estate Solutions revenue rose 83% to S$175.1 million, and the engineering order backlog stands at about S$720 million.
Its net liquid position reached S$313.0 million.
Geospatial is the part to watch.
Revenue there grew 26% to S$150.0 million, helped by the upfront recognition of most of its largest Enterprise Agreement renewal.
Boustead attributed this to the renewal’s licence terms, so the boost may not recur next half.
Why did Valuetronics double its interim dividend while profit fell?
Valuetronics Holdings Limited
(SGX: BN2) is an electronics manufacturing services provider.
For 1HFY2027, it declared an ordinary interim dividend of HK$0.08 per share, double the HK$0.04 paid a year ago.
Separately, it declared a special dividend of HK$0.06, up from HK$0.04.
The bigger payout follows a policy change.
In May 2026, Valuetronics raised its ordinary dividend target to 50% to 70% of net profit, from 30% to 50% previously, and set aside HK$300 million to return to shareholders over FY2027 and FY2028 through special dividends and share buybacks.
Revenue grew, but profit did not.
Revenue rose 7.3% YoY to HK$897.3 million as Industrial and Commercial Electronics (ICE) sales climbed 18.6% to HK$837.9 million.
Consumer Electronics revenue fell 54.3% to HK$59.4 million after the company phased out traditional consumer lifestyle products.
Profit attributable to owners declined 3.5% to HK$89.8 million.
Gross margin narrowed to 18.7% from 19.7% on higher component costs.
Income tax expense rose 50.9% after a Vietnam subsidiary moved from a full tax exemption to a 50% tax reduction.
Management expects ICE revenue to keep growing in FY2027, but that is subject to uncertainty over US trade and economic policies.
Still, the group expects to remain profitable.
A company that doubles its ordinary
dividend
while profit slips leaves itself less room for error.
That said, it held HK$1.15 billion in net cash as at 30 September 2026.
Get Smart: Sort the growth before you count it
A dividend increase is only as durable as its source.
Before you celebrate a higher payout, split it into two piles.
The first pile holds growth the business earned through higher profits and wider margins.
The second holds timing effects and one-offs, such as upfront revenue or a special dividend.
Tiong Woon’s increase sits mostly in the first pile, though its capex needs watching.
Boustead’s sits across both.
Valuetronics paid more while earning less.
So here is the question for you: if next year’s profit only matches this year’s, which of these dividends would still grow?

title: Asian stocks to rally as Huang’s return revives AI
article:
(Nov 24) : Asian stocks looked set to ride a wave of optimism sparked by Jensen Huang’s return to lead Nvidia Corp., a stunning development that propelled Wall Street toward its best day since April 2025.

Equity-index futures for the tech-heavy markets of South Korea and Taiwan pointed to gains of at least 7% at the open. Nvidia shares soared 31%, the most since 2003, helping the S&P 500 climb 4.7% and snap a seven-day losing streak. The Nasdaq 100 surged 6.9%, pulling back from the brink of a bear market, while a gauge of semiconductor shares jumped 14%. Futures for Japan pointed lower as trading resumes after a long weekend.

Nvidia’s board reinstated Huang after a series of meetings and input from “senior levels” of the government. President Donald Trump praised the decision, saying the US has no reason to believe Huang “poses any risk” to national security.

The rally marked a dramatic reversal after the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average entered corrections on Friday. Huang’s ouster after admitting extramarital affairs had thrown the AI trade into turmoil, raising questions about leadership at the company at the center of the boom. His return eased concerns over the outlook for AI investment and whether future profits can justify the industry’s surge in debt-financed spending.

“The reinstatement of the prolific leader of Nvidia’s AI buildout as CEO is bolstering confidence that the momentum of modern technology will remain robust, while sidelining fears of a slowdown,” according to Jose Torres at Interactive Brokers.

Huang returned to Nvidia’s Santa Clara, California, office on Monday to applause and cheers from employees, who shared videos of his arrival. He spoke briefly with workers at one of the entrances.

See also: Stocks jump most since April 2025 as Huang is back

Trump, who personally lobbied Nvidia’s board to reinstate Huang less than two weeks after his dismissal, welcomed his return even as the company continues to investigate the tech titan. “I’ve been speaking to the board directly and indirectly, and I felt very strongly about it,” Trump said during a phone interview with CNBC.

The rally spread across the technology sector. A basket of Magnificent Seven stocks jumped 7.5%, with Apple Inc., Amazon.com Inc. and Tesla Inc. among the gainers. AI-linked companies from Advanced Micro Devices Inc. to Vertiv Holdings Co. also advanced, while CoreWeave Inc., which buys Nvidia chips and rents access to them through the cloud, soared 22%.

“This took me by surprise — shocking!” said Thomas Martin, senior portfolio manager at Globalt Investments LLC. “Jensen drove the market in terms of financing and relationships, but it’s hard to believe the news. We’ll have to see how this develops in the coming days and weeks.”

See also: Asia’s stock rescue efforts gather pace after Wall Street plunge

Short-term Treasuries slipped as the surge in stocks unwound some of the haven demand sparked by last week’s AI selloff. The two-year yield rose about three basis points, while longer-dated Treasuries advanced as falling oil and commodity prices pushed inflation expectations to their lowest levels of the year. Ten- to 30-year yields declined two to three basis points.

“Last week’s AI selloff pushed investors into Treasuries,” said Anna Wu, an investment strategist and founder of Floodlines Research. Now, “some of that safety bid is coming out.”

Oil also fell as investors unwound hedges against an escalation by US forces in Iran amid signs Washington is taking a less hawkish stance for now. West Texas Intermediate dropped around 4% to settle near US$80 a barrel for the first time since August.

On the economic front, US data this week will help shape expectations for the Fed’s December meeting, with consumer confidence due Tuesday, followed Wednesday by the central bank’s preferred inflation gauge, consumer spending and revised third-quarter growth. Signs that price pressures are easing may temper expectations for another aggressive rate increase and provide further support for risk assets.

“We don’t see how the Fed can deliver a 50-basis-point hike in December, or Warsh delivering a hawkish press conference,” said Mohit Kumar, chief economist and strategist at Jefferies. “In our view, the December FOMC should mark the peak in the Fed’s hawkishness and that should clear another hurdle for risky assets.”

title: Stocks jump most since April 2025 as Huang is back
article:
(Nov 25) : An overnight bounce in stocks erupted into the biggest rally since April 2025 after Nvidia Corp.’s reinstatement of Jensen Huang as chief executive officer recharged artificial-intelligence bets.

Shares of the giant chipmaker soared 31%, the most since 2003. Just days earlier, the firm had been at the center of a rout that brought the Nasdaq 100 to the brink of a bear market. The tech-heavy gauge climbed 6.9%. The S&P 500 rose 4.7%. A measure of semiconductor powerhouses jumped 14%.

Nvidia’s board reinstated Huang after a series of meetings and input from “senior levels” of the government. President Donald Trump praised the decision, saying the US has no reason to believe it “poses any risk” to national security.

Huang’s ouster after admitting extramarital affairs had thrown the AI trade into crisis, raising concern about the company at the center of the boom that has fueled big swaths of the economy.

“The reinstatement of the prolific leader of Nvidia’s AI buildout as CEO is bolstering confidence that the momentum of modern technology will remain robust, while sidelining fears of a slowdown,” according to Jose Torres at Interactive Brokers.

Huang returned to the company’s Santa Clara, California office on Monday to applause and cheers from employees who shared videos. He spoke with them briefly at one of the entrances.

See also: Asia’s stock rescue efforts gather pace after Wall Street plunge

While Nvidia’s near-term business fundamentals are the same with or without Huang, it is a fundamentally different stock with him at the helm, according to Joe Tigay at Equity Armor Investments.

“Huang has been an instrumental hype-man, dealmaker, powerbroker, financier and executive for the industry, supporting its expansion and shoring up optimism whenever doubts about massive capital expenditures, uncertain payback prospects and/or integration capabilities surfaced,” said Torres at Interactive Brokers.

His return helps remove a key level of uncertainty around the AI trade, noted Glen Smith at GDS Wealth Management.

See also: Dip buyers hesitate to step in as Nasdaq 100 nears a bear market

“It appears the worst is over and the company can move on from this,” he added. “Corrections can sometimes end as quickly as they begin and we believe the bottom in stocks is likely in.”

title: US stocks soar as Huang’s Nvidia return fuels AI bets
article:
(Nov 24): An overnight bounce in stocks erupted into a surge after Nvidia Corp’s reinstatement of Jensen Huang as chief executive officer recharged artificial-intelligence (AI) bets.

Shares of the giant chipmaker soared 34%, the biggest advance since 2000. A closely watched gauge of semiconductor powerhouses jumped 14%. The S&P 500 rose 5%. The Nasdaq 100 climbed 7%.

Nvidia’s board reinstated Huang after a series of meetings and input from “senior levels of the United States government”. President Donald Trump praised the decision, saying the US has no reason to believe it “poses any risk” to national security.

Huang’s ouster after admitting extramarital affairs had thrown the AI trade into crisis, raising concern about the company at the centre of the boom that has fuelled big swaths of the economy.

“Nvidia’s earnings and near-term business fundamentals are the same with or without Jensen Huang,” said Joe Tigay at Equity Armor Investments. “But as an investment, Nvidia is a fundamentally different stock with Jensen at the helm.”

The decision helps remove a key level of uncertainty from the AI trade, according to Glen Smith at GDS Wealth Management.

See also: Nasdaq 100 has worst week since 2020 on AI drama

“It appears that the worst is over and the company can move on from this,” he said. “Stock market corrections can sometimes end as quickly as they begin and we believe the bottom in stocks is likely in.”

Even before Nvidia’s statement, Morgan Stanley’s Michael Wilson said earnings and valuations were both supportive of a market rebound.

“This is the fat pitch we have patiently been waiting for, and we’re not going to miss it,” he wrote. “Markets bottom on bad news and deleveraging. We have had a lot of both.”

See also: Nvidia turmoil leaves few stock market winners in sea of losers

As investors returned to riskier assets, Bitcoin jumped. Metals also gained. Short-dated Treasuries fell despite a drop in oil prices.
